WASHINGTON (AP) — A claim from the second presidential debate and how it stacks up with the facts:

DONALD TRUMP: “I don’t like Assad at all. But Assad is killing ISIS. Russia is killing ISIS.”

THE FACTS: Not true. Syria’s President Bashar Assad considers the Islamic State group to be among numerous “terrorist” groups that threaten his government, but his military is not fighting them. It is focused on combatting Syrian opposition groups, some of which are supported by the United States. The fight against the Islamic State militants is being waged by a U.S.-led coalition, with help from Turkey, by training, advising and equipping Syrian Arab and Kurdish fighters. While Moscow asserts that it is fighting the Islamic State extremists in Syria, the vast majority of its airstrikes have targeted opposition groups threatening the Assad government.

Daily Devotional

October 10

3 He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not. (Isaiah 53:3 KJV)

It is absolutely amazing that God would let His Son go through what Jesus did. Jesus became a man and felt all the feelings that we do, of rejection, being despised, having sorrows, and acquainted with grief. All so that He could understand how and what we feel as humans, so He could be a perfect High Priest for us (Hebrews 2:17). Jesus did all these things for us, and yet man did not esteem Him, and instead persecuted Him and then crucified Him. Yet, even though man did not treat Him as He deserved, yet He willingly went to the cross for us (Matthew 26:53) – WOW!

If the born again Christian could just understand the unconditional love that God has for us, His children, then he would return that love with everything that he has. The love of God so far surpasses anything we humans have ever felt or understood (Ephesians 3:18-19) that we humans can not really understand it. Our humanity makes us think about ourselves instead of loving our neighbor as ourselves, as Jesus commanded us to do (Matthew 22:39). The fact that God would come to earth, and die for us humans, is amazing. If you can ever realize, and understand, the love of God, then you will be able to love others, as you can not give away what you don’t have. If you truly know the love of God, you will be filled with God, as God is love (1 John 4:8).

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
